artifact_revision: agentmux 2454a0f5 + session-16 working tree (amx 0.8.0, revision 2454a0f5c022-dirty, sha256:ae215d219204, built on the Studio and copied; Agent Mux.app Debug built on the MacBook Pro from the synced working tree, run as a copy under bundle identifier io.github.sglavoie.agentmux.acceptance16); embedded Ghostty 1.3.1; tmux 3.7c (a relocated copy, AgentMux's private server); macOS 27.0.1 on the MacBook Pro
method: One recorded live run from a fresh world, ten cases in order (up crash daemon transfer passive detached sleep exited absent lost): 126 checks, 0 failed (session-16/recovery-acceptance.log ends 'checks passed: 126, failed: 0'). Everything under test ran on Seb's MacBook Pro, by the operator's rule that no UI runs on the Studio: the app copy and its window, the world's daemon, registry and private tmux server (isolated under /tmp/amxs16, no Kitty), and the sleep and wake. The driver (session-16/driver, see its README) ran on the Studio and synthesized NO input on either machine: no key, pointer, VNC, accessibility grant or picture. It starts, quits (Apple event) and kills processes over SSH, moves the app with the same workspace_view request the Dashboard sends (on the world's daemon socket), attaches a second terminal with `amx attach` on a pseudo-terminal, and speaks to the agents with tmux send-keys. It reads the registry, tmux list-clients/list-panes, the daemon's v2 snapshot, `amx attach --json`, the app's saved preferences, the app's unified log, and pmset's power log. The AGENTS ARE STAND-INS, not harnesses (driver/agent.sh installed as the world's `claude`): one managed SessionStart hook, then a count once a second on screen and in a log with PID and clock. 'Same agent' is checked by the registry record, by the operating system's PID and start time of the pane's process, and by a count that never restarts or skips. NOT observed: the pane's pixels (what the pane shows is taken from the app's log, which names each state it enters; the placeholder wording is covered by the hosted WorkspaceRecoveryTests); a real harness; a person at the keyboard; a machine reboot; the Release build; an app upgrade as such (it is the same quit-and-relaunch path). Earlier partial passes while the driver was written are not the record: two checks failed for driver reasons (the Overview starts in a compact layout without previews; a sleep-length threshold was too strict for a sleep broken up by dark wakes). Beside the live run: crash-restart.log (`just crash-restart` on the Studio under -race, 19 scenarios, five of them new against a real tmux server), go-test-ownership.log (internal/tmux ownership and reconcile tests and the cmd/session attach tests, real tmux clients on pseudo-terminals), mac-test-remote.log (the hosted suite on the MacBook through macos/scripts/remote-ui.sh: 364 tests, 0 failures). The MacBook was put to sleep once per sleep run (twice in all) with `pmset sleepnow` and woken over the network; no power setting was changed and nothing was scheduled. The world, the app copy's preferences and /tmp/amxs16 were removed afterwards and no process of the run remains.

app-crash-same-agent.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case app-crash-same-agent, 17 checks, 0 failed). With the app's terminal the one terminal on alpha (107x40) and the app's own saved place `session:<alpha>`, the app (pid 98622) was killed with SIGKILL. Its terminal left the tmux server, the ownership it had recorded was released within 6 s by its `amx attach` outliving the hangup, alpha's pane stayed 107x40, and alpha's agent was the same process before and after (pid 98563, started Sat Oct 10 17:41:14 2026 UTC) and kept counting with no app (14 -> 18). Started again, the new app process logged `reopening at launch (was open: true, place: session:...)`, `session ...: live(clients: 0)` and `restored ...; reattaching its terminal`; one new terminal was on alpha, the agent was still pid 98563 with the same start time, its count never restarted or skipped, and there were still three registrations and three panes.

daemon-restart-same-agent.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case daemon-restart-same-agent, 16 checks, 0 failed). With beta waiting on a permission request, the daemon (pid 98546) was killed with SIGKILL. The app logged the feed gone and `rows held from the last snapshot (3 session(s), selection <alpha>)`; its terminal (client pid 99433) stayed the one terminal on alpha and all three agents kept their PIDs and start times (98563, 98570, 98577). A new daemon (pid 363) was started: the app's feed went live with `rows current (3 session(s), selection <alpha>)`, the new daemon listed the same three runtime-session IDs, beta's waiting state (icon key, attention) came back from the checkpoint with no new hook in hooks.log, the app made no new terminal and let none go, every agent was still the same process with an unbroken count, and no session was launched.

sleep-wake.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case sleep-wake, 14 checks, 0 failed). The MacBook was asked to sleep at 11:43:37 its time (pmset sleepnow) and left alone for 60 s. Its power log shows `Entering Sleep state due to 'Software Sleep'` at 11:43:44, a dark wake and maintenance sleep, and `DarkWake to FullWake` at 11:44:38 after the driver's SSH connection and `caffeinate -u`. The longest pause between two of alpha's once-a-second counts was 29 s while no count restarted or skipped, so the process was suspended with the machine and not replaced. The app logged `woke from sleep; reconnecting the feed` and `feed: live`; the same daemon (pid 363) listed the three sessions; all three agents had the same PID and start time; the same terminal (client pid 4765) was the one on alpha at 107x40; the app made no new terminal; alpha counted on; no session was launched.

detached-operation.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case detached-operation, 12 checks, 0 failed). The app was quit by Apple event while on alpha. No terminal was attached to anything, alpha had no owner on record, and the saved workspace stayed `window_open=1 place=session:<alpha>`. With no app and no terminal, alpha was told to ask for permission and the daemon's snapshot showed it waiting (icon key, attention True); alpha's count went 114 -> 122 in about eight seconds; all three agents kept PID and start time; alpha's pane kept its size; its screen was read with nothing attached. Started again, the app logged `restored <alpha>; reattaching its terminal`, its terminal was the one terminal on alpha, and every agent was still the same process with an unbroken count.

ownership-transfer.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case ownership-transfer, 19 checks, 0 failed). While the app's terminal owned alpha at 107x40, a second terminal ran `amx attach` at 90x25: tmux then listed exactly one terminal on alpha, the second one, the pane became 90x25, the registry named the second terminal's amx as owner, and the app logged `the terminal for <alpha> ended; detached` and `showing detached(...)` and attached nothing in the next five seconds. Quit and started again while the second terminal owned alpha, the app logged `session ...: live(clients: 1)` and `is attached elsewhere (1 terminal(s)); restored detached`, leaving that terminal the only one at 90x25. When the second terminal was closed, no terminal was on alpha, its ownership was released, and the pane stayed 90x25. Started once more with alpha free, the app reattached and the pane was 107x40 again. Alpha's agent was pid 98563 with the same start time throughout and its count never restarted or skipped.

passive-preview-no-resize.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case passive-preview-no-resize, 9 checks, 0 failed). With the app's terminal the only terminal on the server (client pid 2557, on alpha at 107x40) and beta and gamma never attached (80x24), the app's Overview was opened and switched to its preview layout: it showed the current `tick N pid P` lines of all three panes and different lines six seconds later, and the Dashboard's preview showed a pane's screen too. Afterwards the pane sizes were unchanged (107x40, 80x24, 80x24), tmux list-clients was identical (the app's one terminal; none on beta or gamma), no ownership was recorded or changed in the registry, and no pane showed an `echo:` line, which a stand-in prints for anything typed into it.

absent-agent-not-relaunched.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (case absent-agent-not-relaunched, 14 checks, 0 failed). With the saved workspace on beta, the app was quit and beta's agent (pid 98570) killed with SIGKILL while no app ran. The daemon alone recorded beta as `agent exited (signal kill)` and stopped listing it. Started again, the app logged `reopening at launch (was open: true, place: session:<beta>)`, `<beta> is not listed after the restart; asking what became of it` and `<beta> is not running: exited(...); nothing is relaunched`. Eight seconds later the app had made no terminal, none was attached to beta's pane, one stand-in fewer was running with still three registrations and three panes, pid 98570 named no process, a workspace_view request for beta and `amx attach --json` (runtime_session_exited) started nothing, and the app no longer saved beta as its place.

lost-versus-exited.evidence: Observed in session-16/recovery-acceptance.log (cases 'the exit' and 'the loss', 22 checks, 0 failed). EXITED: gamma's agent was told to exit with status 3 while the app showed it; the server kept its pane dead with status 3, the registry recorded `agent exited (status 3)`, the daemon stopped listing it (daemon log: outcome=exited), `amx attach --json` answered runtime_session_exited, and the app logged `session <gamma>: exited(...)`, `is not running: exited(...); nothing is relaunched` and `showing gone(...)`. LOST: the private tmux server (pid 98562) was killed with SIGKILL while the app showed alpha; the app's terminal ended, the registry recorded `backend generation changed`, the daemon logged outcome=lost and stopped listing it, `amx attach --json` answered runtime_session_lost for alpha and still runtime_session_exited for gamma, and the app logged `session <alpha>: lost(...)` and `is not running: lost(...); nothing is relaunched`. Eight seconds later no tmux server answered, no stand-in ran, the registry still held three registrations (one exited by status, one by signal, one lost), and the app had attached nothing.
